MY LEAF STUDIO

My Leaf Rubbing Art

Finish with one big picture made from every rubbing you have made.

Look, then try.

Spread out all your rubbings and choose a big idea: a forest with tall rubbing trees, a rainbow sorted by colour, a leaf family portrait, or a pattern that repeats like wallpaper. Fill the whole page. Layer rubbings on top of each other, try two colours on one leaf and leave some spaces calm and empty. Give your picture a title at the bottom and sign your name like a real artist. When it is finished, hold it up and tell someone about your favourite part.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps with scissors when cutting out rubbings. Collect fallen leaves from the ground, or pick with permission, and brush off dirt and insects. Wash hands after handling leaves. Nothing you find outside goes in your mouth.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My big idea

Choose your idea: a forest, a rainbow, a pattern or something brand new. Sketch the layout lightly.

ACTIVITY 2

Make the picture

Fill the whole box with your rubbings and crayon details. Take your time.

ACTIVITY 3

Gallery time

Give your picture a title and sign it. Then tell someone about it, or describe it here.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Turning separate studies into one composition teaches planning and choice. Naming a picture and explaining it builds pride and confidence in talking about art.
